items.title: EV sales hit records in Australia, Europe as fuel crisis reshapes auto market

featured_image.name: Tesla TSLA Q1 2026 vehicle delivery and production numbers - CNBC

items.description: Soaring gasoline prices driven by the ongoing conflict in Iran are reshaping the global auto market, pushing electric vehicle sales to record highs in several countries and sparking a wave of consumer interest in battery-powered alternatives — even as the picture in the United States remains more complicated.

items.title: Iran severs all diplomatic channels with US ahead of Trump's Hormuz deadline

featured_image.name: Iran war: What is happening on day 39 of US-Israeli attacks?

items.description:
Iran on Tuesday shut down all diplomatic and indirect communication channels with the United States, according to the state-run Tehran Times, in a dramatic escalation that came just hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The move effectively closes off avenues for last-minute negotiations as the six-week-old war enters one of its most dangerous phases.[1][2]

"Iran has closed all diplomatic and indirect channels of communication with the United States. Any and all message exchanges have also been suspended," the Tehran Times reported. The Wall Street Journal, citing a Middle Eastern official, reported that the cutoff of direct diplomacy was intended to signal Tehran's disapproval of Trump's threats, though it noted that some mediated discussions may still be ongoing.[3][4][1]

items.title: UK bars Ye from entering country, Wireless Festival canceled

featured_image.name: Ministers reviewing Kanye West's permission to enter UK

items.description:
The British government on Tuesday denied Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, permission to enter the United Kingdom, prompting the immediate cancellation of this year's Wireless Festival in London. The Home Office rejected Ye's application for an Electronic Travel Authorisation on the grounds that his presence would not be "conducive to the public good," according to the BBC.[1][2]

Ye had been announced as the sole headliner for the three-day Wireless Festival, scheduled for July 10-12 in Finsbury Park, where he was expected to perform before roughly 150,000 attendees. Festival Republic, the event's organizer, confirmed the cancellation and said refunds would be issued to all ticket holders.[3][2][4]

items.title: Vance says he's 'here to help' Orban win Hungary election

featured_image.name: HUNGARY-US-POLITICS-DIPLOMACY-VOTE

items.description: Vice President JD Vance arrived in Budapest on Tuesday and openly endorsed Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's reelection bid, while accusing the European Union and Ukrainian intelligence services of meddling in Hungary's April 12 parliamentary elections — claims he made without providing evidence.

items.title: China and Russia veto UN Strait of Hormuz resolution hours before Trump deadline

featured_image.name: UN proposal on opening Strait of Hormuz gets watered down

items.description:
The United Nations Security Council on Tuesday failed to adopt a resolution aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz after China and Russia vetoed the Bahrain-drafted measure, leaving the international community without a diplomatic framework to address Iran's blockade of the waterway just hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Iran to reopen the strait or face strikes on its civilian infrastructure.[1][2]

The resolution, which had been repeatedly diluted over two weeks of negotiations to avoid precisely such an outcome, received broad support from a majority of the 15-member council but could not overcome the vetoes of two permanent members. The vote was held at 11 a.m. Eastern, nine hours before Trump's 8 p.m. deadline, which he set for Iran to agree to a deal or face attacks on its power plants and bridges.[3][4][2][5]

items.title: IOM says nearly 1,000 migrants died in Mediterranean in 2026 so far

featured_image.name: At least 26 refugees and migrants die in shipwreck off Italy’s Lampedusa

items.description: More than 80 migrants are missing after a boat capsized in the central Mediterranean Sea over the weekend, the United Nations migration agency said Tuesday, in what is part of a devastating stretch of shipwrecks that has made 2026 one of the deadliest years for Mediterranean crossings in over a decade.

items.title: US strikes Kharg Island again as war with Iran intensifies

featured_image.name: U.S. strikes reported on Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil ...

items.description: US forces struck military targets on Iran's strategic Kharg Island on Tuesday as the six-week-old war entered one of its most volatile phases, with airstrikes pounding Tehran, Iranian missiles hitting Saudi Arabia and Israel, and President Donald Trump warning that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Iran does not agree to a deal by his 8 p.m. Eastern deadline.

items.title: Eni announces 2 Tcf gas discovery off Egypt's coast

featured_image.name: Chevron, Eni Make "Significant" Gas Discovery Offshore Egypt

items.description: Eni announced on Tuesday a gas and condensate discovery offshore Egypt estimated at about 2 trillion cubic feet of gas in place, the latest in a string of Mediterranean finds by the Italian energy company that includes a separate 1 trillion cubic feet discovery off Libya's coast last month.

items.title: Trump warns 'whole civilization will die tonight' as Iran deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump threatens to strike Iran's infrastructure if Strait of ...

items.description:
President Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran on Tuesday, warning that "a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again" if Tehran does not agree to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his 8 p.m. Eastern deadline. The ultimatum comes on the 38th day of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which began on February 28 with what the White House called "Operation Epic Fury".[1][2][3][4][5]

Airstrikes hit two bridges and a train station inside Iran on Tuesday morning, while Iranian officials called on young people to form human chains around power plants Trump has threatened to destroy. Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, posted on X that 14 million Iranians had volunteered to fight and said he would join them.[2][6]

items.title: Wall Street firm sends analyst into Strait of Hormuz by speedboat

featured_image.name: The 'gimbal' gambit: An undercover analyst exposes the real truth ...

items.description:
Citrini Research, the small Wall Street firm that rattled markets earlier this year with a bearish call on artificial intelligence, has turned its unconventional methods toward the ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz — dispatching a field analyst into one of the world's most dangerous waterways by speedboat to gather firsthand intelligence on Iranian shipping controls.

The firm said it sent an employee referred to as "Analyst #3" to Oman's Musandam Peninsula, where he boarded a GPS-less speedboat and pushed toward the center of the strait armed with $15,000 in cash and concealed recording equipment, according to The Wall Street Journal. The analyst traveled within view of the Iranian coastline, observing drones overhead and Iranian patrol boats operating nearby, before being intercepted and briefly detained. His phone was confiscated, and his observations were later reconstructed during an eight-hour debrief after he returned safely.[1][2]

items.title: Turkish drillship arrives in Somali waters for historic first offshore oil drilling

featured_image.name: Somalia set for 'historic' first offshore oil drilling - Yahoo

items.description: Somalia is preparing to launch its first-ever offshore oil drilling operation, with a Turkish state-owned drillship expected to arrive in Somali waters later this week. The Çağrı Bey, operated by the Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO), is scheduled to reach Somalia around April 10, marking a milestone in a partnership that could reshape the economic prospects of one of the world's poorest nations.[1][2][3]

items.title: Pentagon cancels briefing as Trump's Iran deadline looms

featured_image.name: Pentagon expands firearm access for off-duty military members on base

items.description: President Donald Trump has warned of the "total destruction" of Iran's bridges and power plants if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by midnight GMT on Tuesday, setting the stage for what could become a dramatic escalation in the five-week-old conflict. The Pentagon, meanwhile, abruptly cancelled a scheduled Tuesday morning briefing with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine, offering no explanation.[1][2]

items.title: IEA chief says Middle East war will accelerate renewables shift

featured_image.name: International Energy Agency head says global economy faces 'major ...

items.description:
The worst energy crisis in modern history will ultimately speed the world's pivot to renewable energy, nuclear power, and electric vehicles, International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol predicted in an interview published Tuesday with the French newspaper Le Figaro.[1][2]

Birol described the current energy shock, triggered by the Middle East war and Iran's de facto blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, as "more serious than those of 1973, 1979 and 2022 combined". Yet the IEA executive director said there were "reasons to be optimistic" about how the upheaval would reshape the global energy system.[2][1]

items.title: Dangote refinery ramps up African exports amid Iran war

featured_image.name: Dangote to export maiden petrol cargo out of Africa ...

items.description:
Nigeria's Dangote refinery, the largest in Africa, has stepped up exports of gasoline and urea fertilizer to countries across the continent as supply disruptions caused by the war on Iran continue to squeeze global energy and commodity markets, owner Aliko Dangote said on Monday.[1][2]

The refinery, operating at its full capacity of 650,000 barrels per day, has shipped approximately 17 cargoes of gasoline to other African nations, with urea fertilizer exports also climbing as buyers scramble for alternatives to traditional Middle East and Gulf suppliers, according to Reuters. Dangote said the facility had helped cushion the crisis both in Nigeria and across the continent.[1]

items.title: Iran war energy shock accelerates global return to nuclear power

featured_image.name: Japan to restart world's biggest nuclear plant - Le Monde

items.description: The war between Israel and Iran has upended global energy markets, cutting off roughly one-fifth of the world's liquefied natural gas supply and prompting a rapid reassessment of nuclear energy across Asia and beyond. Countries that had retreated from atomic power after the 2011 Fukushima disaster are now racing to restart reactors, extend plant lifespans, and build new capacity as LNG prices surge and supply reliability crumbles.

items.title: Saudi Arabia closes Bahrain causeway after Iranian missile strikes

featured_image.name: King Fahd Causeway | bridge, Bahrain-Saudi Arabia | Britannica

items.description: Saudi Arabia shut down the King Fahd Causeway, the sole road link connecting it to Bahrain, early on Tuesday as Iranian ballistic missiles targeted the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province, according to the Associated Press. The closure came hours before a deadline set by President Donald Trump for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face strikes on its power plants and bridges.[1][2]

items.title: Oil rises, futures slip as Trump's Iran deadline looms

featured_image.name: US-ISRAEL-IRAN-WAR-POLITICS-TRUMP

items.description: Global markets entered a period of heightened tension on Tuesday as President Donald Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — set for 8 p.m. Eastern Time — loomed over trading floors worldwide. Oil prices climbed while U.S. equity futures slipped, and cryptocurrency markets wavered as investors weighed the prospect of a last-minute diplomatic breakthrough against the threat of a devastating military escalation.

items.title: King Fahd Causeway reopens after Iranian missile strikes on Saudi Arabia

featured_image.name: Saudi Arabia shuts key King Fahd Causeway linking Bahrain ...

items.description:
The King Fahd Causeway, the sole road link between Saudi Arabia and the island kingdom of Bahrain, reopened on Tuesday after a brief closure prompted by Iranian ballistic missile strikes targeting Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. The King Fahd Causeway Authority announced on X that traffic on the bridge was "back to normal after a temporary suspension" that had been imposed as a precautionary measure.[1]

The reopening came hours after authorities halted all vehicle movement across the 25-kilometer bridge in the early hours of Tuesday, as Iran launched seven ballistic missiles toward Saudi Arabia's eastern region. Saudi Arabia's defense ministry said it intercepted and destroyed the missiles, though debris fell near energy facilities. A major fire erupted at the Al Jubail Industrial City, the Middle East's largest industrial hub and a center of petrochemical and oil refining operations, after what open-source intelligence accounts described as a ballistic missile and drone attack.[2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: Air India, WestJet raise fuel surcharges as Iran war doubles jet fuel costs

featured_image.name: Air India to raise fuel surcharge amid rising jet fuel ...

items.description: Two major carriers on opposite sides of the globe announced fuel surcharge increases this week as the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign in Iran continues to roil global energy markets. WestJet will introduce a temporary $60 surcharge on companion voucher bookings starting April 8, while Air India is overhauling its surcharge structure for both domestic and international flights effective April 8 and April 10, respectively.[1][2]

items.title: Trump's Tuesday deadline for Iran looms as oil markets surge

featured_image.name: Trump appears to extend Iran deadline in cryptic post - Le Monde

items.description: Oil markets swung wildly on Monday as President Donald Trump issued his most forceful ultimatum yet to Iran, demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday evening or face devastating strikes on the country's infrastructure. U.S. crude briefly exceeded $114 per barrel before retreating, while premiums for physical barrels of American oil climbed to record levels as buyers across Asia and Europe scrambled for supply.[1][2]
